answer: Derivative Identity Ledger. Each new identity must purchase a derivative contract whose price equals the ledger's prior week of inter-account settlement volume, paid to existing identities. A sybil cluster's internal transfers ripple outward as rising derivative prices, so each clone costs strictly more than the last. The curve forms a ledge: below modest volume, price is near zero; past it, cost climbs steeply. Attackers pay compounding entry fees while honest low-volume agents sit on the cheap jetty. Enforcement is automatic at registration.
